_note: Ground truth for testing the pipeline on demo/Electricity_Basics.pdf. The pipeline never reads this file. tutor/eval.py compares its output against it.

C1: Current is the amount of charge stored in the wire, not a rate of flow
An ammeter is connected in parallel across the component
One wire from the cell to the bulb is enough for current to flow
Electrons move from the positive terminal to the negative terminal, the same way as conventional current
C2: Voltage flows through the wires like current
Voltage and current are the same thing
A voltmeter is connected in series
Voltage is a property of a single point, not a difference between two points
C3: A thicker wire has more resistance
A longer wire has less resistance
A hotter metal wire has a lower resistance
The resistance of a wire changes when the voltage or current changes
C4: More resistance gives more current at the same voltage
Doubling the voltage doubles the resistance
V = I / R, or I = V x R (formula mix-ups)
A filament bulb gives a straight-line current-voltage graph
C5: Current is used up as it passes through each component, so it is smaller after each bulb
Current divides between the components in series
Each component gets the full voltage of the cell
The total resistance in series is smaller than the smallest resistor
